Avis de sollicitation de manifestations d’intérêt pour le recrutement d’un Consultant (Firme) pour l’Évaluation Environnementale et Sociale Stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga, Province du Kasai Centrale en République Démocratique du Congo.

AMI N°                                      : ZR-PURUK-543648-CS-QCBS

Date de publication : 11 juin 2026

Date de clôture : 25 juin 2026

Source de financement               : Banque mondiale (Crédit IDA N° 72160-ZR)

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale (BM) à hauteur de 100 millions USD pour financer le Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga (PURUK). Le Ministère de l’Urbanisme et de l’Habitat, à travers l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK, envisage d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour couvrir les paiements relatifs au recrutement d’un consultant cabinet ou firme en charge de l’évaluation environnementale et sociale stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga.

2. Les prestations du Consultant consistent à : (i) Réaliser une Évaluation Environnementale et Sociale Stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) Ville de Kananga, et (ii) élaborer une Étude d’Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisme (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) de la Ville de Kananga.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK invite, par le présent avis d’appel à manifestation d’intérêt, des candidats firme éligibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience pertinente requises pour exécuter la mission.

4. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : (i) le consultant doit être une société, un cabinet ou un bureau d’études spécialisé dans les évaluations environnementales et sociales, (ii) disposer d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience dans les études environnementales et sociales, (iii) il (elle) doit prouver document à l’appui qu’il (elle) a déjà réalisé, seul ou en tant que chef de fil d’un groupement, au cours de sept (7) dernières années (2019-2026), au moins deux (2) missions similaires (EESS) de programmes ou stratégies de développement urbain et au minimum trois (3) EIES de projets financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers. Une expérience en RDC sera très fortement valorisée.

5. La durée de la mission est de cent (100) jours.

6. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 des règlements de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2023, qui énoncent la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

7. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût telle que décrite à la Section VII, paragraphe 7.3 du règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2025.

Les consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et ou d’une sous-traitance

8. Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires (les termes de références) à l’adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 16 heures locales et sur le site Media Congo.

9. Les manifestations d’intérêt, écrites en langue française doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier, accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou PDF copiable sur une clé USD ou envoyé par courrier électronique en format PDF copiable aux adresses : ugpuruk@gmail.com, jeanmichelmbungu@gmail.com et spm.puruk.cosmos@gmail.com au plus tard le 25 Juin 2026 à 00h00', Heure locale de Kananga (TU+2), et porter clairement la mention : AMI N° : ZR-PURUK-543648-CS-QCBS – Recrutement d’un consultant cabinet ou firme en charge de l’évaluation environnementale et sociale stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga en République Démocratique du Congo.

L’adresse est l’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga « UG-PURUK », A attention de : Monsieur Jean Michel MBUNGU NGUMBA, Coordonnateur ai. 601, Avenue Gécamines, Quartier Malandji, Commune de Kananga, Ville de Kananga, Province du Kasaï Central, République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Téléphone : +243 992905752 / +243 823 041 704.

MBUNGU NGUMBA Jean Michel

REQUEST FOR THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

International Individual Consultant (Intermittent)

Strengthening the Internal Audit Capacity of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport

Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project Phase 1

 

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) has applied for financing support from the World Bank's (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project (CRCI) with and duration of six (6.5) years starting in early 2027. The CRCI consists of the following 4 components:

Component 1: Road Corridor Improvement

Component 2: Institutional Capacity Strengthening in Logistics and Trade Facilitation

Component 3: Phase 1 Project Management and Phase 2 Preparation

Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response

 

MPWT is responsible for overall technical supervision, execution and management of the Project.

 

The CRCI seeks to enhance transport connectivity along Cambodia's segment of Asian Highway 21 (AH21), a key east-west corridor linking Cambodia and Viet Nam. Upgrading this section will promote economic growth in Cambodia's northeastern provinces and strengthen trade relations with neighboring countries. The project aims to improve community road access to essential services, including health centers, referral hospitals, schools, and markets, by upgrading climate-resilient national roads. Additionally, it will lower transportation costs and mitigate risks of road disruptions, thereby supporting the efficiency of agricultural supply chains and promoting tourism development within the project area. The CRCI will use the Output and Performance Based Road Contract (OPBRC) approach to support upgrade, climate resilience, safety, and maintenance for parts of NR 64, NR 62, all of NR 9, sections of NR 7 and NR 78.

 

Objective of the Assignment:

The objective of this consultant assignment is to support MPWT to strengthen its internal audit capacity for establishing and operationalizing a sustainable, risk-based internal audit function in MPWT that delivers:

  1. Risk-based audit programs and execution, focusing on high-risk areas of CRCIP
  2. Practical audit tools and manuals, aligned with GDIA and IIA standards
  3. Staff training to enhance detection and reporting of fraud and integrity risks, including red flag identification.
  4. Support improving internal regulations for Improved quality and consistency of internal audit outputs, supported by basic quality assurance mechanisms.

 

Consultant Profile and Qualifications:

The selected Individual Consultant should meet the selection criteria set out below:

  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Economics, or related field with 15 years of general experience. Professional certification such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), CPA, ACCA, or equivalent is strongly preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of relevant international experience in internal audit, financial management, or related assurance functions, preferably in the public sector.
  • Demonstrated experience with min. 3 projects in building internal audit capacity in government institutions, including developing audit manuals/SOPs and delivering training/coaching.
  • Strong knowledge and hands-on application at least 5 years of international internal audit standards and good practices (IIA/IPPF), including risk-based internal audit planning and QAIP.
  • Experience at least 3 projects with externally financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB or other development partners) and familiarity with financial management and procurement risk areas in donor-funded operations is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, communication, report writing, and stakeholder engagement skills, and ability to work effectively with government counterparts.
  • Ability to work in hybrid mode (on-site and remote) and deliver outputs within agreed timelines.

 

The RGC, through the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) and its Project Management Unit (PMU), is seeking to engage one (1) qualified International Individual Consultant to support the PMU-CRCI during the project preparation phase 1. 1. Background

The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km2) of land mass in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient electricity infrastructure.

 

MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government. Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support.

 

RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050. As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources.

 

Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025.  In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI.

 

IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and MEC.

 

IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to:

 

  • Energy Act 2025
  • National Energy Authority Act, 2025
  • Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034
  • Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s development
  • MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build
  • National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date
  • Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication.

 

The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and support the integration of renewable energy.

2. Objectives

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation.

 

  • Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions.
  • Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE promotion, and e-mobility uptake.
  • Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and implementation gaps.
  • Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information.
  • Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower.

3. Project Description

This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.

4. Implementation Arrangements

 MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance. NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:

 

  • MEC management and technical staff
  • REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable
  • Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC
  • NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant
  • Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation
  • World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support
  • ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant

Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment.

5. Scope of Services

The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement, data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's technical acceptance.

 

  • Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands

The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework.

  1. Review of existing applicable  policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025,
  2. Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and
  3. Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps.

 

  • Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national commitments and targets

The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets, initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic review will include the following:

  1. Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress,
  2. The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives, and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI,
  3. Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets,
  4. Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing framework, and
  5. Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps.

 

  • Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps 

The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following:

  1. Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation,
  2. Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue,
  3. Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025,
  4. Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework,
  5. Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed (short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies,
  6. Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps.
  7. Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework, and
  8. Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2 and in this Task, and compile the recommendations.

 

The roadmap should indicate:

  • Short-term actions,
  • Medium-term actions,
  • Long-term actions,
  • Responsible institution,
  • Required decision or instrument,
  • Dependency,
  • Level of priority, and
  • Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment.
  • Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector

The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities, aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant will examine the following:

  1. Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB,
  2. The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and
  3. Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC.

 

The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant shall assess:

  1. Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders,
  2. Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving (proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE, EE and E-MB for the next 5 years,
  3. Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and
  4. Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for international collaboration, certification).

 

 

 

  • Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE

The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will:

  1. Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems),
  2. Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions, reporting frequency, and validation process,
  3. Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and
  4. Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update and improve upon.

 

  • Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations

The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and other stakeholders.

 

The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. The Consultant shall, in particular:

  1. Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms;
  2. Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility financial, operational and investment data;
  3. Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated under the relevant sections of the Energy Act;
  4. Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network, resilience and access investments;
  5. Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations;
  6. Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment;
  7. Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework;
  8. Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes;
  9. Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations;
  10. Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands, estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration;
  11. Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government subsidies, and the alternatives available;
  12. Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply;
  13. Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging;
  14. Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can accommodate;
  15. Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities, including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed;
  16. Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and
  17. Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and Billing Code.

 

  • Task 7: Addressing the recommendations

Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.

The Consultant shall, in particular:

  1. Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts, including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards, universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms,
  2. Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration, renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids,
  3. Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts,
  4. Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements, and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and
  5. Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant institutions for implementation.

 

6. Qualifications, Tasks, and Level of Effort of Specified Key Experts

The Consultant shall propose a team adequate for the assignment. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify:

  • Each proposed key personnel position,
  • The name of the proposed expert, where available,

  • Whether the input is international or national/local,

At a minimum, the Consultant is expected to consider the inclusion of expertise and an indicative level of effort and split of on-site and remote deployment, as follows:

7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses

As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:

  • A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months or person-days), provided for information purposes; and
  • Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel, accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for the performance of the services.

The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.

8. Deliverables

The project has six (6) main deliverables.

 

The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services. The Task references identify the principal Tasks contributing to each deliverable and shall not limit the Consultant's obligation to take into account relevant findings and recommendations arising from other Tasks.

  1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (Linked to: Tasks 1 to 7)

The Consultant shall submit an Inception Report confirming its understanding of the assignment, methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement arrangements, data and information requirements, and detailed schedule for carrying out the seven Tasks and submitting the required deliverables.

An Inception Workshop shall be conducted with MEC, NEA, and other relevant stakeholders, and agreed outcomes shall be reflected in the final Inception Report.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within two weeks of Notice to Proceed (NTP).

  1. Deliverable 2: Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap (Linked to: Tasks 1, 2 and 3)

The Consultant shall prepare a consolidated Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap for the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, relating to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility.

The deliverable shall consolidate the diagnostic and strategic reviews, identify and categorize the principal implementation, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps and misalignments, and establish a prioritized, time-bound roadmap to address them.

The roadmap shall identify responsible institutions, required actions, sequencing, dependencies, priorities, and the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines to be prepared or aligned under this assignment.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within ten weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 3: Institutional and Capacity Development Framework (Linked to: Task 4 and relevant institutional findings from Tasks 1 to 3)

The Consultant shall prepare an Institutional and Capacity Development Framework setting out the recommended institutional arrangements, roles and responsibilities, coordination arrangements, manpower and skills requirements, identified capacity gaps, and capacity-development strategy for RE, EE and e-mobility.

The proposed framework shall be consistent with the findings and priorities established under Deliverable 2

The Deliverable shall be submitted within eighteen weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework and RE Report (Linked to: Task 5)

The Consultant shall prepare the Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for monitoring progress in RE, EE and e-mobility, including the recommended database, data collection, validation and reporting arrangements and institutional responsibilities.

The deliverable shall include the recommended database and reporting arrangements and the first RE Report, prepared in a form suitable for subsequent updating by NEA.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6)

The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6.

The deliverable shall provide the analytical and regulatory basis necessary to support tariff-related decisions and the preparation or implementation of the applicable tariff and billing regulatory framework.

The deliverable shall also include the updated tariff model in editable form, covering all MEC-served systems including Ebeye, and concise briefing notes setting out the rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff positions, for use by MEC and NEA in policy and stakeholder discussions.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act (Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3)

Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the assignment.

The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and guidelines covering, as applicable:

  • Electricity-sector regulation;
  • Renewable energy;
  • Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and
  • E-mobility.

The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP.

 9. Contract Duration

The contract duration is 9 months. The expected start date is January 2027. 

10. Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and the REGAIN Procurement Plan. Interested firms shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience. EOIs will be evaluated against the criteria below. The most qualified and experienced firm will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if responsive, to negotiate a contract.

  • Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
  • Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
  • Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)

Total: 100 points

Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage. The qualifications of the proposed key experts set out in Section 6 will be reviewed when the selected firm submits its technical proposal.

11. Inputs to be provided by MEC and NEA

MEC, as the Employer, and NEA, as the technical and regulatory counterpart, shall provide or facilitate timely access to the information, documents, data, personnel, and stakeholders reasonably required for the performance of the Services, to the extent available.

NEA shall:

  • Provide or facilitate access to applicable policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, regulatory instruments, sector targets, reports, databases and other relevant regulatory information,
  • Provide available information on institutional arrangements, regulatory processes, staffing and capacity relevant to the assignment,
  • Facilitate access to relevant officials and stakeholders for consultations and workshops, and
  • Review and provide timely technical comments and acceptance of deliverables submitted to it for review or acceptance.

MEC shall:

  • Provide or facilitate access to relevant technical, operational, customer, commercial, financial and investment information and data, including information required for the tariff review, covering all MEC-served systems including Ebeye (former KAJUR operations), and MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model,
  • Provide available plans, studies, reports, databases and information relating to existing and planned RE, EE, e-mobility, storage, and network,
  • Facilitate access to relevant MEC and PMU personnel and stakeholder consultations, and
  • Undertake the contractual, administrative and financial review and approval of deliverables in accordance with the implementation arrangements.

The Consultant shall, as part of the Inception Report, submit a consolidated data and information request specifying the information required, its proposed source, format and required date. The Consultant shall promptly identify material data gaps and propose appropriate alternative sources, assumptions or methodologies where required.

The provision of information by MEC, NEA or any other stakeholder shall not relieve the Consultant of its responsibility for the verification, analysis, adequacy and quality of the Services and deliverables required under the Contract.

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS N° 072/PASEA/2026

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT/FIRME POUR L’ASSISTANCE DU MINHAS ET DE L’ONEP DANS LE CADRE DU SUIVI DE LA MISE EN ŒUVRE ET DES INDICATEURS DE PERFORMANCE DU CONTRAT DE DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC (DSP) DE L’EAU POTABLE

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire a obtenu un crédit de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA), d’un montant équivalent à deux cent cinquante millions (250 000 000) USD, pour la préparation du Projet d’Appui à la Sécurité de l’Eau et de l’Assainissement (PASEA). Une partie de ces ressources financières sera utilisée pour le paiement de contrat des prestations de services de consultant pour le recrutement d’un consultant/firme pour l’assistance du MINHAS et de l’ONEP dans le cadre du suivi de la mise en œuvre et des indicateurs de performance du contrat de délégation de service public (DSP) de l’eau potable.

L’objectif de cette mission est de proposer un mécanisme de suivi pour assurer un appui opérationnel immédiat et un renforcement durable des capacités du MINHAS et de l’ONEP dans le cadre du suivi de la mise en œuvre et des indicateurs de performance du Contrat de Délégation de Service Public (DSP) de l’eau potable, conformément aux exigences du PAD du PASEA et aux dispositions contractuelles en vigueur.

Il s’agira pour le Consultant/firme de :

  • appuyer le MINHAS et l’ONEP dans le suivi et la vérification des indicateurs de performance du Contrat de DSP ;
  • développer et opérationnaliser les outils de suivi, d’analyse, de contrôle, ainsi que de régulation économique et financière indépendante ;
  • renforcer la capacité d’analyse critique des données transmises par l’opérateur privé ;
  • structurer les rapports annuels et triennaux d’évaluation de la performance du Contrat de DSP ;
  • Suivi reproché annuel de la production (en prenant en compte aussi les producteurs indépendantes), volumes facturés et non facturé, la rémunération, titrisations et dette annuelle du secteur.
  • mettre en œuvre un programme de transfert progressif de compétences au profit des cadres du MINHAS et de l’ONEP.

La durée de la mission est de trente-six (36) mois y compris les délais de validation des livrables.

2. Le présent avis à manifestation d’intérêt a pour objectif de solliciter des firmes compétentes en vue d’établir une liste restreinte dans le cadre du recrutement d’un consultant/firme pour l’assistance du MINHAS et de l’ONEP dans le cadre du suivi de la mise en œuvre et des indicateurs de performance du contrat de délégation de service public (DSP) de l’eau potable.

3. L’Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Appui de Sécurité de l’Eau et à l’Assainissement (UC-PASEA) invite les firmes intéressées à manifester leur intérêt pour les services décrits ci-dessus. Les firmes intéressées doivent fournir un dossier comportant une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt et les informations pertinentes indiquant qu’elles sont qualifiées pour exécuter les prestations demandées (brochures, références concernant la bonne exécution de contrats similaires, expérience dans des conditions semblables, années de réalisation, coûts, clients). 

Le Consultant/firme devra être un cabinet ou bureau d’études légalement constitué, justifiant d’une existence légale d’au moins cinq (5) années à la date de soumission des offres. Il devra disposer d’une expérience confirmée et documentée dans les domaines de la régulation des services publics d’eau, de l’analyse et du suivi des contrats de délégation de service public (DSP), ainsi que du suivi et de l’évaluation des indicateurs de performance technique, financière et commerciale des opérateurs de services publics.

Le Consultant/firme devra avoir réalisé, de manière satisfaisante, au moins cinq (05) missions similaires au cours des dix (10) dernières années, portant spécifiquement sur :

  • au moins deux (02) missions intégrant un volet structuré de renforcement des capacités et de transfert de compétences institutionnelles au profit d’administrations publiques ou d’autorités délégantes.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI)

Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Project:-Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project (MESSP) – Preparation Grant for Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project 

Project ID:-P516394 Grant No. E6970-ET 

Assignment Title:- Hiring of a Project Manager for PIU

Reference No.ET-ESS-574077-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) has received financing from the World Bank and intends to apply part of the proceeds to recruit an individual consultant under the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) method.

The project aims to improve the availability, quality, timeliness, and use of official statistics for evidence-based policymaking in Ethiopia. ESS will establish a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) responsible for day-to-day implementation, including coordination, procurement, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social risk management, reporting, annual work planning and budgeting, procurement planning, and liaison with the World Bank and key stakeholders.

 2. Assignment Objective

The Project Manager will provide overall leadership and management of the PIU to ensure effective, efficient, and compliant implementation of project activities in accordance with the Financing Agreement, Project Implementation Manual, annual work plans, procurement plans, fiduciary requirements, environmental and social commitments, and World Bank procedures.

3. Scope of Services / Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager shall, among other duties:

- Provide overall strategic leadership, direction, and management of the project. 

- Coordinate the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, procurement plans, training plans, ICT modernization plans, and project budgets. 

- Ensure timely implementation of project activities in accordance with approved project documents, financing agreements, and implementation schedules. 

- Lead and coordinate digital transformation and ICT modernization initiatives under the project, aligned with ESS strategic priorities and national digital transformation agendas. 

- Coordinate technical, fiduciary, safeguards, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), ICT, and administrative functions of the PIU. 

- Serve as the primary liaison between ESS and key institutions including the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Ministry of Planning and Development (MoPD), sector ministries, development partners, and the World Bank. 

- Ensure compliance with World Bank procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, digital governance, cyber security, and reporting requirements. 

- Supervise consultants, specialists, and support staff recruited under the project, including ICT and digital transformation specialists. 

- Facilitate coordination with sector institutions to strengthen data integration, interoperability, and administrative data systems. 

- Lead the preparation and submission of quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project progress reports. 

- Organize and coordinate Steering Committee and Technical Committee meetings. 

- Monitor project implementation progress and recommend corrective actions where necessary. 

- Identify project risks (including ICT-related risks) and oversee mitigation measures. 

- Ensure stakeholder engagement, communication, and change management activities. 

- Perform any other related duties assigned by ESS management.

4. Duration and Duty Station

Duration:-18 months, full-time, subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. 

-Duty Station:-ESS Headquarters, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The project preparation phase will be up to eighteen (18) months from the date of hiring. Implementation is expected to commence upon Project Effectiveness and continue for approximately five (5) years, with possible overlap between preparation and implementation phases.)

5. Minimum Qualifications and Experience

Education:-

- Master’s degree or above in Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Public Administration, Project Management, Development Studies, ICT for Development, or related field.

Professional Experience:

- Minimum ten (10) years of relevant professional experience, including at least five (5) years in project coordination/management/program management roles. 

- Demonstrated experience managing large-scale, multi-stakeholder, donor-funded development projects. 

- Proven experience coordinating and implementing World Bank-financed projects is mandatory (experience with other multilateral/bilateral donors is an added advantage). 

- Demonstrated experience in ICT modernization, digital transformation, e-government, statistical modernization, or data system strengthening initiatives. 

- Strong understanding of digital technologies, data ecosystems, information systems, administrative data integration, interoperability frameworks, and digital governance principles. 

- Proven experience working with PIU and managing multidisciplinary teams (procurement, financial management, safeguards, ICT, and M&E). 

- Strong knowledge of World Bank operational policies and procedures including procurement, financial management, safeguards, M&E, and reporting requirements. 

- Experience with national statistical systems and public sector institutions is highly desirable.

6. Selection Method

The consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method.

7. Submission of Expression of Interest

A titre de régularisation,

La date limite de soumission des plis était fixée au 30 juin 2026.

  1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), financé par la Banque mondiale, le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de l’Innovation Technologique (MTNIT) lance un Avis à manifestation d’Intérêt en vue du recrutement d’un cabinet spécialisé.

La mission porte sur la réalisation d’une Etude d’Impact Environnemental et Social Simplifiée (EIEES) des travaux de rénovation à l’ESATIC.

L’objectif de l’étude est (i) d'identifier aux niveaux environnemental, social, sanitaire et sécuritaire, les éléments sensibles du sous-projet, (ii) de déterminer les interventions du sous-projet susceptibles d'avoir des impacts sur l'environnement et les communautés, (iii) d’évaluer les risques et impacts potentiels du sous-projets et (iv) de recommander des mesures et actions de bonification des impacts positifs et d'atténuation des impacts négatifs afin de garantir la durabilité environnementale et sociale du sous-projet.

  1. Profil du cabinet

Les cabinets intéressés devront justifier :

  • d’un agrément délivré par le Ministère en charge de l’Environnement ;
  • d’au moins cinq (05) missions d’études environnementales et sociales (EIES, CIES, NIE, EESS, CGES) de projets/programmes d’infrastructures (construction / réhabilitation d’écoles, aménagement ou construction d’établissement recevant du public, etc.) financés/cofinancés par les partenaires techniques et financiers (Banque mondiale, BAD, AFD, BID, BOAD, etc.) et du secteur privé ;

Ces expériences devront être prouvées par des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution fournies par le commanditaire de l’étude.

  • de la disponibilité d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire comprenant au minimum :
    • un chef de mission, Spécialiste en Environnement de niveau d’étude minimum BAC+5 ans en gestion de l'environnement ou des ressources naturelles ou domaine équivalent (géographie, biologie, foresterie, etc.) ;
    • Un (1) Expert Sociologue, Anthropologue, Socio-économiste ou évaluation sociale ;
    • Un (1) Ingénieur des travaux publics ou en Génie Civil ;
    • Expertise supplémentaire lorsque nécessaire.

La durée de la mission est estimée à quarante-cinq (45) jours calendaires pour la réalisation de la mission de terrain.

Les cabinets intéressés devront solliciter l’intégralité des Termes de Références aux courriels suivants : juliekoffi2@yahoo.com, avec en copie obligatoire à bernardkoffi1@gmail.com et  padci@telecom.gouv.ci.

  1. CONSTITUTION ET DEPOT DES MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

Les manifestations d’intérêt soumises par les cabinets ou groupements de cabinets devront comprendre :

-  Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée et cachetée ;

-  en cas de groupement, un accord ou un projet d’accord de groupement signé et cacheté ;

-   la présentation du cabinet (son existence légale, organigramme, personnel) ;

-  les Curriculum Vitae des spécialistes et la copie de diplômes sont exigés ;

-  la copie du RCCM ou tout autre document équivalent pour les entreprises étrangères ;

 - les preuves de l’expérience du cabinet relatives à l’exécution de missions similaires, les Attestations de Bonne Exécution ou fiche projet ou certificat de service fait.

 Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposées sous pli fermé comprenant cinq (05) exemplaires dont un original, et une version électronique (sur clé USB ou tout autre support électronique portant clairement la mention « Manifestation d’intérêt pour le recrutement d’un cabinet (firme) pour la réalisation d’une Etude d’Impact Environnemental et Social Simplifiée (EIESS) » à n’ouvrir qu’en séance d’ouverture des plis le mardi 30 juin 2026 à 10 heures GMT à l’adresse géographique ci-dessous :

O Governo de Angola, através do Ministério da Administração Pública, Trabalho e Segurança Social (MAPTSS), por via do Instituto Nacional de Emprego e Formação Profissional (INEFOP) e com o apoio do Banco Mundial, recebeu um financiamento no valor de 250 milhões de dólares americanos para a implementação do Projecto de Emprego e Oportunidades para Jovens em Angola (AYEOP/JOVEM+, P505158), aprovado pelo Conselho de Administração do Banco Mundial em 20 de Março de 2025, e pretende aplicar parte deste financiamento na Contratação de um Assistente de Gestão de Riscos Sociais.

O Ministério da Administração Pública, Trabalho e Segurança Social (MAPTSS), é o responsável pela fiscalização e implementação do projecto. Para o efeito, será constituído dentro do INEFOP uma Equipa de implementação do projecto (EIP) que assumirá as responsabilidades de governança, aquisições, gestão financeira e salvaguardas ambientais e sociais do projecto e outras, na qual, o Director Geral do INEFOP irá actuar como coordenador, responsável pela gestão das actividades.

O objectivo da contratação é de apoiar técnica e operacionalmente o Especialista Social e a EIP na implementação, monitoria, documentação e reporte das medidas de gestão de riscos sociais do Projecto Jovem+, contribuindo para uma implementação inclusiva, participativa, não discriminatória, transparente e coerente com os instrumentos ambientais e sociais do Projecto, legislação angolana aplicável e Normas Ambientais e Sociais do Banco Mundial.

O Projecto AYEOP/JOVEM+, convida os consultores individuais elegíveis para manifestarem o seu interesse em fornecer os Serviços. Os Consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante para executar os Serviços.

Os critérios de seleção são:

  1. Licenciatura em Ciências Sociais, Sociologia, Serviço Social, Psicologia, Antropologia, Desenvolvimento Social, Estudos de Género, Gestão de Projectos, Direito humanos ou área afim.

Formação em matéria de género, direitos humanos, desenvolvimento social ou gestão de projectos será vantagem.

  1. Domínio da gestão de riscos ambientais e sociais e das Normas Ambientais e Sociais do Banco Mundial /NAS2/NAS10, MGSR, PEPI ou VBG/EAS/AS.
  2. Domínio de Word, Excel e ferramentas digitais de gestão de informação.
  3.  Mínimo de 3 anos de experiência relevante em desenvolvimento social gestão de riscos sociais, inclusão, ou áreas relacionadas;
  4. Experiência comprovada de trabalho em matérias relacionadas como: Gestão de Reclamações, Envolvimento de Partes Interessadas, Violência Baseada no Género, inclusão, gestão laboral, monitoria ou reporte;
  5. Experiência em projectos financiados pelo Banco Mundial e/ou outros parceiros será vantagem.
  6. Conhecimento do contexto angolano e disponibilidade para deslocações às províncias.
  7. Experiência com dados sociais, Excel e relatórios.

 

Os Consultores deverão ter em especial atenção a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 dos Regulamentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (o “Regulamento de Aquisições”), datadas de Setembro 2025, que estabelecem as políticas do Banco Mundial relativas a conflito de interesse.

  • Curriculum Vitae actualizado, contendo informação detalhada sobre a formação académica, experiência profissional e principais actividades desenvolvidas, particularmente as relacionadas com o objecto da contratação;
  • Referências profissionais, incluindo contactos de anteriores empregadores, instituições ou responsáveis que possam confirmar a experiência e o desempenho profissional do candidato;

  • Comprovativos de experiência profissional relevante, quando aplicável, tais como declarações de serviço, certificados de trabalho, contratos ou outros documentos equivalentes;
  • Outros documentos que possam ser solicitados no âmbito do processo de selecção e contratação.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT: SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CARRY OUT NATIONAL TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ON EUROTRACE TO FOUR (4) SADC MEMBER STATES. BW-SADC-563150-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/465

 

DATE OF ISSUE:                   20 October 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services for Conduct National Training and Technical Assistance on Eurotrace to Four (4) SADC Member States, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to Conduct National Training and Technical Assistance on Eurotrace to Four (4) SADC Member States (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  12 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to train Member States on the use of statistical software for merchandise trade statistics.

 

  1. Specific objectives

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake an advance national training on EUROTRACE, especially SQL server based EUROTRACE to Statistics Agencies of four (4) SADC Member States to process and analyse trade data. Another objective is to provide technical assistance on assessment of the EUROTRACE system challenges faced by National Statistics Agencies.

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results:

  1. Strengthened technical capacity of Statistics Agencies in four (4) SADC Member States in the effectively and efficiently management and processing of trade  data using SQL Server based EUROTRACE;
  2. Sources of challenges with EUROTRACE identified, documented and resolved; and
  3. Statistics Agencies in four (4) SADC Member States to process and disseminate trade statistics using Eurotrace (SQL).

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant as the Master Trainer and strong experience and there should be evidence of in-depth knowledge of EUROTRACE. The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

  • A minimum of a Degree in statistics, economics, IT, Data Science or related field, A Master’s degree and above shall be an advantage.
  • Certificate in training on EUROTRACE
  • Written and oral fluency in the English language is essential. 
  • Excellent oral and written communication, analytical, presentation and report writing skills in English Language. 
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills to prioritize workload and delivery needful during the training week.

 

General Professional Experience

  • The Expert Must have at least fifteen (15) years of experience in merchandise trade statistics compilation and dissemination.

 

Specific Professional Experience

  • Demonstrated experience of at least 10 years using EUROTRACE for processing and dissemination of merchandise trade statistics at national, regional or continental level;
  • Demonstrated experience as a resource person in delivering at least 5 training/technical assistance activities to developing countries at national, regional and continental level in Eurotrace software. Training in SADC Member States shall be an advantage.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be engaged for 12 months. The assignment is for a continuous period of twelve (12) months from the date of contract signature. This is a calendar-based duration and does not represent an accumulation of individual billable days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to four (4) SADC Member States.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:            SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO UNDERTAKE CAPACITY BUILDING ON STATA IN FIVE (5) SADC MEMBER STATES AS A RESOURCE PERSON. BW-SADC-563171-CS-INDV

 

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: SADC/5/2/466

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 20 October 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to undertake capacity building on Stata in five (5) SADC member states in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to undertake capacity building on Stata in five (5) SADC member states (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  12 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to enhance the capacity of Member States on collection, processing and analysis of census, surveys and administrative data.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake a national training on STATA to five (5) SADC Member States National Statistics Offices to process and analyse censuses, surveys  and administrative data, specific to each country.

 

Furthermore, the objectives are also to:

 

  • strengthen the technical capacity of National Statistics Offices staff in using STATA for advanced statistical analysis, focusing on Official Statistics.
  • promote the use of do-files and automation techniques to improve efficiency, traceability, and standardization of analysis processes.

 

  • assess the existing practices and use of STATA by the different departments of National Statistics Offices and encourage adoption of common methodologies across technical departments, ensuring coherence, quality, and statistical comparability

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following result:

  • Strengthening technical capacity of National Statistics Offices in the management and processing of data from census and surveys using STATA; and 
  • Identification of gaps regarding use of STATA by the different departments of National Statistics Offices to roll out the gaps to close specific timelines and associated tasks. 

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant as the Master Trainer and there should be evidence of in-depth knowledge with statistical analysis software (STATA).  The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of master’s degree in statistics, economics, IT or related field
    • Written and oral fluency in the English language is essential.  Knowledge of French and/or Portuguese is an added advantage.
    • Excellent oral and written communication, analytical, presentation and report writing skills in English Language. 
    • Excellent time management and organizational skills to prioritize workload and deliver needful during the training week.

 

General Professional Experience

    • The Expert Must have at least ten (10) years of experience using statistics analysis software STATA pertaining to Official Statistics.

 

Specific Professional Experience

    • Proven experience in statistical data processing and analysis, spatial analysis, modelling and data visualization using STATA for at least 3 major surveys for Official Statistics at national level;
    • Experience in the design and implementation of training materials for the conduct of statistical data analysis training in Official Statistics using STATA;
    • Extensive experience as a resource person in delivering at least 3 training on STATA at national level, particularly using household and census data.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 12 months. Note: the 12 months is the duration of the assignment and not the number of days required to undertake it. It caters for coordination of work to be done by recipients of the assignment and to a certain extent, flexibility for the consultant to deliver on the outputs.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to five (5) SADC Member States.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : «recrutement d'un consultant national pour l'appui technique à la mise en œuvre de l'enquête trimestrielle sur l'emploi et le secteur informel au Congo (EESIC-T)».

2. L'objectif général de la mission est d'apporter un appui technique de haut niveau à l'Institut National de la Statistique pour la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l'exploitation de l'Enquête Trimestrielle sur l'Emploi et le Secteur Informel au Congo (EESIC-T), en garantissant la qualité de l'opération conformément à la méthodologie harmonisée de la CEMAC et en assurant une production périodique d'indicateurs fiables et comparables sur le marché du travail et le secteur informel.

Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira de :

  • Appuyer la finalisation des documents techniques et des outils de collecte (questionnaires ménage, emploi, secteur informel, fiche de dénombrement, manuels d'instructions, protocole d'enquête) en étroite collaboration avec l'expert international du BIT et l'équipe technique permanente ;
  • Contribuer à la conception et au paramétrage de l'application CAPI utilisée pour la collecte des données, ainsi qu'à la définition des règles de cohérence, des filtres et des sauts ;
  • Appuyer le tirage de l'échantillon trimestriel et la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du panel rotatif (renouvellement d'un tiers de l'échantillon chaque trimestre) sur la base du plan de sondage aréolaire à deux degrés ;
  • Contribuer à l'organisation et à l'animation des sessions de formation des superviseurs, contrôleurs et enquêteurs, ainsi qu'à la conduite de l'enquête pilote ;
  • Assurer le suivi technique des opérations de collecte trimestrielles, le contrôle qualité des données (suivi des entretiens, contre-interviews, contrôles automatiques) et l'accompagnement méthodologique des équipes terrain ;
  • Participer au traitement, à la pondération et à l'analyse des données collectées, ainsi qu'à la production des tableaux de résultats et des indicateurs clés du marché du travail ;
  • Veiller à l’archivage des bases de données trimestrielles apurées et pondérées ;
  • Veiller à la mise à jour des tableaux de bord trimestriels des indicateurs clés du marché du travail et du secteur informel ;
  • Contribuer à la rédaction des rapports trimestriels et annuels d'analyse des résultats de l'enquête ;
  • Assurer l'interface technique permanente avec l'expert international du BIT et intégrer dans les travaux nationaux les orientations méthodologiques internationales.
  • Etc…

3. L’Unité de gestion du projet HISWACA invite les consultants individuels à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations sur leur qualifications et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations (curriculum-vitae daté et signé, copies des diplômes et des justificatifs de références en prestations similaires réalisées, etc.)

5.  Les consultants peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission par courriel à l’adresse : ugp@hiswaca-congo.org/ recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com , de 9 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 16 heures (heures locales) du lundi au vendredi.

6. Procurement Process: Selection of Consultants — CQS (Firm)

1. Background

The Federal Government of Nigeria, supported by the World Bank through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, is implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project. The Project Development Objective is to improve water security in Nigeria by enhancing the management and resilience of water resource infrastructure, increasing water availability for irrigation and hydropower, improving dam safety, and promoting institutional collaboration for climate-resilient food and energy production. This assignment relates to Components 2 (Irrigation Modernization) and 3 (Improvements in Dam Operations and Enhancing Dam Safety) of the Project.

The Kware Irrigation Scheme, in Kware Local Government Area of Sokoto State, spans approximately 500 hectares within a broader 10,000-hectare irrigation zone supplied by the Kware–Shalla Dam. An Environmental and Social Screening exercise conducted in 2025 classified the Scheme as Category A (High Environmental and Social Risk), with High social sensitivity driven by the proximity of the Giro community to the dam, flood risk to surrounding communities, and the potential for physical or economic displacement during rehabilitation. The SPIN Project target is full rehabilitation and operationalisation of 600 hectares, with planned works including raising of the dam embankment by one metre, construction of a spillway control well, a second (emergency release) pipeline, and rehabilitation of the main and distributary canal network.

Given the scale and nature of these works, a site-specific Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) is required, consistent with the disclosed SPIN Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement, and the Nigerian Land Use Act. The Sokoto State Ministry of Agriculture and Natural Resources, through the SPIN Project Implementation Unit (the "Client"), now wishes to engage a qualified firm to prepare the RAP.

2. Objective and Scope of Services

The objective of the assignment is to identify potential physical and economic displacement risks and impacts associated with the rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, and to prepare a comprehensive, site-specific RAP that avoids, minimises, mitigates, and manages displacement and livelihood impacts, in compliance with the Nigerian Land Use Act and World Bank ESS5. The Scope of Services includes, but is not limited to:

  1. Review of project documents, engineering designs, and applicable national legal frameworks, with a gap analysis between Nigerian law and ESS5 and proposed bridging measures;
  2. A 100% census and detailed socio-economic survey of Project Affected Persons (PAPs), disaggregated by sex, age, and vulnerability status, and a 100% inventory of affected assets (land, structures, crops, trees, and common property);
  3. Establishment of a formal cut-off date, supported by public notification, and use of GPS, GIS, and satellite imagery in asset surveys and mapping;
  4. Preparation of an Entitlement Matrix and full-replacement-cost compensation rates, with particular attention to eligibility criteria that are advantageous to women and other vulnerable groups;
  5. Design of a detailed livelihood restoration framework, including vocational training, income-generating activities, and special provisions for vulnerable groups;
  6. A stakeholder consultation and disclosure strategy, a site-specific Grievance Redress Mechanism, and measures to address impacts on host communities;
  7. A detailed, costed, and time-bound RAP implementation schedule linked to civil works milestones, institutional implementation arrangements, and a monitoring and evaluation framework, including provision for an independent RAP Completion Audit.

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) describing the detailed scope, methodology, deliverables, and reporting requirements will be provided to shortlisted firms.

The assignment shall not exceed eight (8) weeks from the date of contract signing.

Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  1. The firm must be an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm with a minimum of five (5) years' work experience in projects requiring resettlement planning and implementation;
